utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-98-32-PT, Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner representing the Prosecution, together with Ann Sutherland, legal officer, and Andrew Powell, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honour, Vladimir Domazet, lead counsel of Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is a Status Conference to be held in accordance with the Rules and I think within time. How are you going, Mrs. Korner, in the discovery matters?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In respect of the disclosure of the statements, all statements obtained which were referred to on the last Status Conference have been disclosed to the Defence, both in English and in the Bosnian language. Can I perhaps move on to an associated matter in respect of those statements?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All of those statements have been disclosed with the identity of the witnesses redacted, as is the expression here. Your Honours issued an order -- can I just get the correct date of that order? -- I think on the 8th of September -- yes -- that the Prosecution, and I quote paragraph 2: "Is to comply on or before the 6th of October 2000 with an obligation under Rule 66(A)(i) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence to supply to each of the accused copies, in unredacted form, of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment and confirmation was sought."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That, I'm afraid, is the perils of using a precedent. There's only one accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. And indeed, I think part of the perils of using a precedent arises as well from our original motion, because Your Honours may have got the impression that -- from paragraph 3 of the original motion dated the 27th of January, that the Prosecution had made redactions of material that had gone before the Confirming Judge. We hadn't. The material which went before the Confirming Judge was, in fact -- did not disclose the identities of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You said that on the previous occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In those circumstances, if Your Honours were aware of that, we had, in fact, complied with our obligation under Rule 66(A) because the material which the Defence have got is the identical material seen by the Confirming Judge. I understand the spirit of Your Honour's order. It is very similar, if not identical, to an order you issued in the case of Brdjanin and Talic. But I've spoken to Mr. Domazet this morning about that, and his view is that he does not require, at this stage, the identity of the witnesses. His defence is, in fact, as he's made very clear to us, one of alibi. All that I'm pointing out is that if the Defence don't require it and we have, in fact, complied with our obligations under Rule 66, if Your Honours still feel that you wish to issue an order that we should disclose the identities, I think it would have to be a separate order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Let's hear what Mr. Domazet says about it. Mr. Domazet, you don't require, at this stage, the identity of those witnesses who gave statements and which were before the Confirming Judge; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. For the moment, as far as I am concerned, the identity of the witness is not of the greatest importance, and I am not making a problem out of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Ms. Korner, you can rest assured that we won't have to debate, on this particular occasion, the obligation of the Prosecution to reveal, at least to the Confirming Judge, the identity of the witnesses. So that can arise, no doubt, in some later stage if there is the new ploy adopted by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not a ploy, Your Honour, with the greatest of respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry to laugh. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour knows, of course, that we do have strong feelings about protection of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's right. But at some stage, you are going to have to reveal the witnesses' identity if you have revealed them to the Confirming Judge or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely, and we intend to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you going to make an application for protective measures in relation to any witnesses? Because you have to serve any other statements as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honour, all statements that we're going to use have been served on the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But are they ones in addition to those which were before the Confirming Judge?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then, we better find out from Mr. Domazet whether he wants the identity for those as well. He may well not. Mr. Domazet, in relation to the other statements, that is, those which were not before the Confirming Judge, do you require the identity of those witnesses at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Ms. Korner, that means you've complied with 66(A)(1) and 66(A)(2), have you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HUNT
utterances.text: Now, on the last occasion, you told us that the pre-trial brief was in the process of being prepared and that it would be filed shortly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. It hasn't been filed yet. It is in the process of being prepared. I cannot say exactly how long it would take, but obviously we're in Your Honour's hands on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the Trial Chamber is not able to give any real indication as to when this case will come on for hearing, but it is one which, we are all aware of, will take a very short time. And hopefully during some break in the next case -- there is always some form of break whilst the Defence gets ready or something -- we could take it then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I realise it will be jumping the list, but there's no point in starting something like Brdjanin and Talic and then putting it aside for another three or four months. So this is obviously one which, if we can, we will fit into one of those breaks. So my own feeling is that it could well get a run early next year, so that's why we need to have the pre-trial brief when you have it so that we can get on with the final preparations. You are also going to interview the accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Again, very helpfully, I'm spoken to Mr. Domazet this morning about that. He would like to be able to read before the interview, which his client is agreeable to, the new material which he's just received. He, I understand, also has other aspects to his professional life which may make it a little difficult for him to get to deal with it until sometime in October. If it's suitable, the agreeable date would be mid-November for the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's a matter between the parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We can't make orders for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. But the only reason I say that is, it would probably be more helpful to serve -- whatever the expression is -- the pre-trial brief after the interview has been conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. By that stage, you may also have some agreed facts, one hopes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, your obligations under 68, of course, are ongoing --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- exculpatory material.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And you understand the Defence is one of alibi.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So we understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm just looking to see what other ones have to be notified. The so-called special defence of diminished responsibility, or what might be called insanity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't -- I have no indication that that's going to be applicable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, alibi and those would be rather hard to run together, I should think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know. It's been done, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, it's been done in a trial I had before a jury, which was rather remarkable. Well, there's no point in dealing with the names of any of the Defence's witnesses because you haven't revealed yours. Well, not given them a list yet. Any other matters that you feel should be raised at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Mr. Domazet, any matters you want to raise in the terms of the order -- of the rule in relation to your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. At this point in time, no, thank you. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are very grateful to the parties for being so cooperative, it's a pleasure to see, and hopefully we'll get this case on and over with speedily at the beginning of next year sometime.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Obviously, Your Honours can't give an exact date, but Your Honours are working on the basis it may come in early next year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, what I hope to do, and it will depend upon how Krnojelac runs, there's always a period of some weeks between the end of the Prosecution case and the beginning of the next one -- and for once I'm grateful to see the Prosecution hasn't got identical teams on consecutive cases -- so that would be the ideal time for a short case like this. Now, your estimate was 14 days for the Prosecution case. Even allowing the same amount for the Defence case, we should be able to get through it in a month, one would hope.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may have to be fitted in with the other case, if it's still going, when they're ready to start their defence, but it's obviously a case which should be got out of the way as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm grateful for that indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No doubt you'll be in touch with those in Krnojelac to see how it's running, and there will probably have to be another Status Conference within the meaning of the rules before it comes up, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much to counsel, and for your assistance. We will adjourn.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
